# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

- **CI failure root cause** (fetched via `dmtools github_get_workflow_run_logs` for run `38090372517`, since `ci_failures_full.log` was not present in `input/`): the `CRAP + duplication` (guards) job died on its FIRST step — the CRAP ratchet:

  13.00  100.0  N/A   13  (top-level)._runAgentLoop   lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart:1042
  Max CRAP: 13.00 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)
  ```

  Both functions were pushed to cyclomatic complexity 13 by this PR's additions, exceeding the 12.0 threshold pinned in `crap4dart.yaml` (ratchet only moves down). The `Quality gate` aggregate failed solely because `guards = failure` (confirmed in its log: `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is failure (guards)`); all other legs were green.
- **No open review threads** (`pr_discussions_raw.json` → `"threads": []`), no merge conflicts — pure CI fix.
- The subsequent guards steps (baseline quality gates, loc gate, jscpd, dupx) never ran in CI because the ratchet step failed first under `bash -e`; all were reproduced locally (below).

## Approach

Behavior-preserving complexity extractions — no logic change, no contract change (TDD: the existing finalize-gate suites already cover both functions at ~100%, they serve as the regression net and stay green):

1. **`lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`** — `_ledgerSpans` (CC 13) is now a small dispatcher (CC 4) over two new single-shape scanners, each carrying half the decision points:

   - `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` (CC 6) — unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets near-miss scan (blank-tolerant entry run).
   - Shared return shape: private record typedef `_SpanScan = ({_LedgerSpan span, int nextLine})`.
2. **`lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`** — the end-of-run FinalizeGate fold block moved out of `_runAgentLoop` (CC 13 → 8) into a new top-level `_emitFinalizeGateFold(newMessages, contextMessages, emit)` (CC 6): emit `TaskLedgerEvent` only when produced state + ledger, rewrite the terminal answer in both `newMessages` and the context transcript when stripped. Guard call site is one line: `if (currentConfig.finalizeGate) await _emitFinalizeGateFold(...)`.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — `_ledgerSpans` split into dispatcher + `_fencedLedgerSpanAt` / `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` (+ `_SpanScan` typedef).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart` — extracted `_emitFinalizeGateFold`; `_runAgentLoop` gate block replaced by a one-line call.

## Test Coverage

- **RED reproduced locally** before the fix: `crap4dart 0.11.0 analyze` (same version CI activates) reported CC 13 for both offenders.
- **GREEN after the fix**: re-measured — `_runAgentLoop` CC 8, `_ledgerSpans` CC 4, new helpers CC 7/6, `_emitFinalizeGateFold` CC 6; no repo function above CC 12 (the ratchet's pinned ceiling) — the whole-repo max returns to 12.00.
- `crap4dart check --baseline` → 3 passed, 1 warned (the pre-existing, warning-severity duplication triage debt; the two new scanners produced no new findings).
- jscpd duplication guard: **0.81% < 1.0% PASS** (the two duplicate pairs touching `agent_loop.dart` are pre-existing tool-call boilerplate, untouched by this change).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1523
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1523
- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +538
- **Deletions**: -125
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:04:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# gh-1516: [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

## Symptom (owner report, session 01a12772-de61-77e1-b3c9-332394827a86, ai_conf/demo)

Interactive TUI, `approvalMode: autopilot`, trivial question ("почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"):

- verification ritual around a plain-text answer: writes its own reply to `/tmp/fa_reply.txt`, `sed` it back, `stat -f %m` both files to "measure response time" — 4+ pointless shell calls, several as background jobs;
- the reply carries a visible "Checklist (требования и верификация)" section and an **unfenced `task-ledger` dump** (requirement/command/expected/actual/status).

Same setup with haiku answered the same class of question normally — so the trigger is universal, the explosion is model-dependent (weak models take imperative prompts literally).

## Root cause (owner direction: the PROMPT, not the mode wiring)

`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (gh-1412) says "Before ANY final summary you MUST: checklist → verify each item with a real command → ledger" with **no scoping by turn type**. "Verify produced state" presumes the model can judge that a pure chat turn produced no state — gpt-5-mini can't; it verifies the act of answering itself. The prompt never says when the contract does NOT apply.

(Secondary, kept for completeness: the gate is wired to `approvalMode == unattended` at agent_cli.dart:649 — but per owner direction the fix belongs in the prompt: a chat turn must not trigger the ritual in ANY mode.)

## Requirement

1. **Self-scoping prompt**: finalize_gate.md opens with an explicit applicability rule — the contract applies ONLY to turns that produced artifacts or state changes (files written/edited, commands that mutate, services/configs touched). Pure discussion / Q&A / explanations / status answers → answer directly, NO checklist, NO verification commands, NO ledger. Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a "why did you…" question, a "what does X do" question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules.
2. **Tolerant strip**: `finalize_gate.dart` must also catch the near-miss shapes models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet list) — parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown.
3. Never-again REG: scripted-provider test where a trivial question in a gate-active session yields zero tool calls and no checklist/ledger in the visible transcript; unfenced-ledger strip unit tests.

## Acceptance

- Gate-active session (any mode): trivial Q&A → direct answer, zero verification calls, clean transcript.
- Gate-active session with real produced state: full gh-1412 contract intact (checklist, real verification, fenced ledger parsed + persisted).
- Bench/unattended behavior for real tasks unchanged.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

# Pull Request Information

- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +538
- **Deletions**: -125
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:04:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# gh-1516: [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

## Symptom (owner report, session 01a12772-de61-77e1-b3c9-332394827a86, ai_conf/demo)

Interactive TUI, `approvalMode: autopilot`, trivial question ("почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"):

- verification ritual around a plain-text answer: writes its own reply to `/tmp/fa_reply.txt`, `sed` it back, `stat -f %m` both files to "measure response time" — 4+ pointless shell calls, several as background jobs;
- the reply carries a visible "Checklist (требования и верификация)" section and an **unfenced `task-ledger` dump** (requirement/command/expected/actual/status).

Same setup with haiku answered the same class of question normally — so the trigger is universal, the explosion is model-dependent (weak models take imperative prompts literally).

## Root cause (owner direction: the PROMPT, not the mode wiring)

`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (gh-1412) says "Before ANY final summary you MUST: checklist → verify each item with a real command → ledger" with **no scoping by turn type**. "Verify produced state" presumes the model can judge that a pure chat turn produced no state — gpt-5-mini can't; it verifies the act of answering itself. The prompt never says when the contract does NOT apply.

(Secondary, kept for completeness: the gate is wired to `approvalMode == unattended` at agent_cli.dart:649 — but per owner direction the fix belongs in the prompt: a chat turn must not trigger the ritual in ANY mode.)

## Requirement

1. **Self-scoping prompt**: finalize_gate.md opens with an explicit applicability rule — the contract applies ONLY to turns that produced artifacts or state changes (files written/edited, commands that mutate, services/configs touched). Pure discussion / Q&A / explanations / status answers → answer directly, NO checklist, NO verification commands, NO ledger. Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a "why did you…" question, a "what does X do" question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules.
2. **Tolerant strip**: `finalize_gate.dart` must also catch the near-miss shapes models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet list) — parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown.
3. Never-again REG: scripted-provider test where a trivial question in a gate-active session yields zero tool calls and no checklist/ledger in the visible transcript; unfenced-ledger strip unit tests.

## Acceptance

- Gate-active session (any mode): trivial Q&A → direct answer, zero verification calls, clean transcript.
- Gate-active session with real produced state: full gh-1412 contract intact (checklist, real verification, fenced ledger parsed + persisted).
- Bench/unattended behavior for real tasks unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

- **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +538
- **Deletions**: -125
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:04:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# gh-1516: [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

## Symptom (owner report, session 01a12772-de61-77e1-b3c9-332394827a86, ai_conf/demo)

Interactive TUI, `approvalMode: autopilot`, trivial question ("почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"):

- verification ritual around a plain-text answer: writes its own reply to `/tmp/fa_reply.txt`, `sed` it back, `stat -f %m` both files to "measure response time" — 4+ pointless shell calls, several as background jobs;
- the reply carries a visible "Checklist (требования и верификация)" section and an **unfenced `task-ledger` dump** (requirement/command/expected/actual/status).

Same setup with haiku answered the same class of question normally — so the trigger is universal, the explosion is model-dependent (weak models take imperative prompts literally).

## Root cause (owner direction: the PROMPT, not the mode wiring)

`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (gh-1412) says "Before ANY final summary you MUST: checklist → verify each item with a real command → ledger" with **no scoping by turn type**. "Verify produced state" presumes the model can judge that a pure chat turn produced no state — gpt-5-mini can't; it verifies the act of answering itself. The prompt never says when the contract does NOT apply.

(Secondary, kept for completeness: the gate is wired to `approvalMode == unattended` at agent_cli.dart:649 — but per owner direction the fix belongs in the prompt: a chat turn must not trigger the ritual in ANY mode.)

## Requirement

1. **Self-scoping prompt**: finalize_gate.md opens with an explicit applicability rule — the contract applies ONLY to turns that produced artifacts or state changes (files written/edited, commands that mutate, services/configs touched). Pure discussion / Q&A / explanations / status answers → answer directly, NO checklist, NO verification commands, NO ledger. Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a "why did you…" question, a "what does X do" question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules.
2. **Tolerant strip**: `finalize_gate.dart` must also catch the near-miss shapes models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet list) — parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown.
3. Never-again REG: scripted-provider test where a trivial question in a gate-active session yields zero tool calls and no checklist/ledger in the visible transcript; unfenced-ledger strip unit tests.

## Acceptance

- Gate-active session (any mode): trivial Q&A → direct answer, zero verification calls, clean transcript.
- Gate-active session with real produced state: full gh-1412 contract intact (checklist, real verification, fenced ledger parsed + persisted).
- Bench/unattended behavior for real tasks unchanged.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

content.thinking:
Now I have the full diff. Let me examine key files in full to find issues:

1. `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart` — full content, especially `_isLedgerHeading` and `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` (blank-line swallowing concern), `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` (parse twice → O(n²) perf but fine).
2. `lib/src/agent_loop.dart` — `_emitFinalizeGateFold` context message rewrite, `messages.any` for producedState — wait: producedState computed on `messages` passed in = `newMessages` — check.
3. `agent_cli.dart` — `_agent.finalizeGate = config.headlessRun;` — check `headlessRun` semantics: is `fa wire-serve` headless? PR description notes wire-serve is not a `-p` run so gate stays off. But other hosts: bench runs `fa -p`. What about `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` — is it true also for `fa serve`? The PR notes that wire-serve keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode. But wait — the credential-hunt nudge AC5 (from AGENTS.md) — `AgentCoreServices.isUnattended` is keyed on LIVE approval mode, deliberately different. OK.

Potential issues to consider:

A. **`stripTaskLedger` / parseTaskLedger double scanning**: `_emitFinalizeGateFold` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)`, each runs `_ledgerSpans` (O(n)). Minor perf, negligible for final answers. Also parse called per text block.

B. **`_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` blank tolerance**: blanks "may separate entries", but the loop breaks on the FIRST non-blank non-entry line. Consider:

```
## task-ledger
- requirement: a
  command: x

some prose paragraph

- requirement: b
```

The scan breaks at "some prose paragraph" and the span ends at requirement a. Then `- requirement: b` later is a dangling entry — never included. This means the last ledger of the doc could be only partial. Also, the `_entryLine` regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` matches any bullet with `key: value` — e.g. a regular markdown bullet "- requirement: see the docs" in normal prose right after a `## task-ledger` heading would be parsed. That's the intended tolerant behavior though.

C. **More serious**: `_entryLine` matches at ANY indentation, including deeper-indented bullets that are part of a list item's nested content. Also `_fieldLine` `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` requires at least one leading whitespace — matches any indented line with `key: value`... wait, it would also match `  - requirement: x`? No, `- requirement` starts with `-` not a letter. OK.

Actually the pre-existing parse had the same grammar inside the fence; the tolerance extends it outside. Prose false-positive test exists ("the task-ledger record is persisted hidden" — inline, rejected since token must be alone on line). Good.

D. **`_isLedgerHeading`**: `token = line.trim()`, handles `#` prefix strip via regex `'^#{1,6}\s*'`. What about heading like `## **task-ledger**` (bold inside heading)? Not handled — token after `#` strip = `**task-ledger**`, then bold check handles it. Order: strip `#` first, then bold. Good. What about `###task-ledger` (no space)? `^#{1,6}\s*` matches zero spaces, so `###task-ledger` → `task-ledger` ✓.

E. **Blank-line runaway in `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt`**: blanks are skipped but never end the span — so:

```
## task-ledger
- requirement: a
  command: x
  status: pass

(the agent continues writing many paragraphs…)

- requirement: stray mention: something
```

The scan breaks at first prose line. OK fine.

But wait — a subtle bug: blanks are consumed inside the while loop without updating `lastEntry`, and the scan only ends at a non-blank non-entry line or EOF. That means the span `nextLine = j` could skip blank lines and the strip removes [startLine, lastEntry]. Fine.

F. **`stripTaskLedger` blank-collapse behavior mutates surrounding text**: it collapses ALL blank runs in the whole answer (not just around the removal site). Original:

```
Para 1.


Para 2 (double blank between paragraphs)
```

If a ledger exists somewhere, stripTaskLedger collapses the double blank between Para 1 and Para 2 into a single blank — and trims leading/trailing blank lines of the entire answer. So stripping is NOT confined to the ledger site. The test `stripTaskLedger leaves plain answers byte-identical` only covers no-ledger case. Is this a BLOCKING? It's a behavioral wart: the final answer text gets reformatted beyond the ledger removal. For a "transcript never shows it" requirement, it changes the visible answer formatting. Probably IMPORTANT at most — it's a minor cosmetic overreach. Hmm, but the doc comment says "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated" — the implementation collapses ALL runs, not just the removal site. That's a discrepancy between comment and code. I'd call it IMPORTANT (or SUGGESTION). The answer shown to user differs in whitespace. I'd classify SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT. Let me think about severity per guidelines: "IMPORTANT — real maintainability or correctness issue." It could misrepresent the model's formatting... minor. I'll go SUGGESTION... Actually the loop-test expects `text.trimRight(), 'Task complete.'` — works either way. I'll flag as IMPORTANT? The comment explicitly claims only edges; the code does global collapse. Deviation from documented behavior = correctness nit. SUGGESTION is fine given low impact. Hmm, let me flag as SUGGESTION.

G. **`_emitFinalizeGateFold` context rewrite**: `currentContext.messages` — is the context list the same list object mutated later/persisted? Replacing by identity: `contextMessages.lastIndexWhere((m) => identical(message, fold.original))`. The original message object came from `newMessages` — but is the terminal assistant message in `contextMessages` identical to the one in `newMessages`? Depends on loop implementation: `newMessages` are the run's new messages; context messages list presumably already contains them (appended as produced). If `identical` fails (e.g., messages are copied when appended to context), the context rewrite silently doesn't happen, and the session record would still show the ledger. Let me check the loop code to see how newMessages relate to context.messages.

Also: mutation of `newMessages[fold.messageIndex]` — but `AgentEndEvent(List.unmodifiable(newMessages))` is emitted after, so events carry the stripped message ✓ (test verifies).

But there's a potential issue: the assistant message was ALREADY emitted via a MessageEvent (assistant message event) earlier in the run — hosts may have persisted/rendered the unstripped message already, and then a later event carries the stripped version. In the CLI, is the assistant message persisted at emit time or at end? Need to check agent_loop event flow: does an AssistantMessageEvent fire for the final message before the fold? If hosts persist messages on the event, then the fold's mutation happens after persistence → session JSONL still contains the unstripped ledger, and only the context in-memory copy is replaced. The PR claims "the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it" — need to verify how the CLI persists assistant messages. Let me check.

H. **`producedState` detection**: `messages.any((m) => m is AssistantMessage && m.content.any((block) => block is ToolCall))` — newMessages only contains messages of this run. A turn where the model called tools counts as produced state even if tools were read-only (`read` of key.txt in persist test — read is not state-changing). Per the prompt, "no state-changing commands" — the loop can't know; any tool call = produced state approximation. Acceptable approximation? The ticket acceptance: "trivial Q&A → zero tool calls". A read-only turn with ledger would still fire the event — fine. But note the test added a `read` tool call to make the event fire, and the prompt says "produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands". Slight mismatch between prompt scoping (state-changing) and loop scoping (any tool call) — a read-only turn would carry the full contract per the loop (event + strip) but the prompt says skip. Minor inconsistency, arguably intentional approximation. Could flag as SUGGESTION.

I. **`_foldTaskLedger` iterates text blocks reversed and returns on FIRST block that parses** — matches old `_finalTaskLedger` behavior (last text block wins). ✓. But note: old code returned null after checking the first assistant message (loop `return null` after first assistant message check)... Old code: iterate reversed; first non-assistant → return null; check that assistant message's blocks; then `return null`. New: only checks `messages.last`. Same semantics since reversed iteration means the last message decides anyway (if last is assistant, old code checks it and returns null without looking further; if last is not assistant, returns null). Equivalent ✓.

J. **Unchanged `_errorToolResult` reformat** — pure formatting churn from `dart format`. Noise in diff; fine.

K. **agent_cli.dart**: `_agent.finalizeGate = config.headlessRun;` — check where `headlessRun` is defined and whether `fa wire-serve`/`fa serve`/`fa hub serve`/`fa trajectory` headless commands set it. If some unattended headless flows (e.g., `fa serve`) don't set headlessRun, gate silently off — PR notes this explicitly for wire-serve and asks reviewers to flag if wire runs should count. That's a deliberate documented decision — SUGGESTION-level at most; they asked. Also `dap` flows.

Wait, more important: is there any OTHER place that sets `finalizeGate`? grep for `finalizeGate =` in repo. Also `isUnattended` for credentialHuntNudge still keyed on approval mode — unchanged, per AGENTS.md that's intentional (live approval mode). But now there's an inconsistency: an interactive autopilot session has `isUnattended == true` (credential nudge on) but `finalizeGate == false`. That's documented as intentional in AGENTS.md.

L. **bench behavior**: bench runs `fa -p` → headlessRun true ✓ per PR notes. Let me verify `AgentCliConfig.headlessRun` is set from `-p` in bin/fah.dart and bench harness.

M. Check the ticket requirement #1: "Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a 'why did you…' question, a 'what does X do' question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules." The prompt addition says: "**Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise." — NO negative examples included! The ticket explicitly required 2-3 negative examples in the prompt. The PR instead relies on: (a) the prompt rule, (b) the wiring fix (gate only headless). The AC: "Gate-active session (any mode): trivial Q&A → direct answer". Hmm — is this a ticket-AC gap? The requirement #1 says "Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt". The added text has one parenthetical example "(a pure question answered from what you already know)" — that's abstract, not concrete examples like "why did you…". This is a deviation from the ticket requirement. Given owner direction in the ticket ("Root cause (owner direction: the PROMPT, not the mode wiring)") — the owner explicitly wanted the fix in the prompt with examples. The PR primarily fixed the WIRING (headlessRun keying) and added only an abstract rule without the requested concrete negative examples. This is a scope/requirement deviation worth flagging as IMPORTANT (ticket requirement not fully satisfied).

Hmm wait, let me re-read the ticket requirement: "1. Self-scoping prompt: finalize_gate.md opens with an explicit applicability rule ... Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a 'why did you…' question, a 'what does X do' question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules."

The PR description says the fix includes the trivial-turn clause. The clause is abstract with a single generic parenthetical. No concrete negative examples. Also "opens with an explicit applicability rule" — the rule was appended inline to the first paragraph, not really "opens with" — it's in the opening paragraph, fine.

So: gap vs ticket requirement #1 (concrete negative examples missing). The PR's actual mechanism for interactive sessions is the wiring change, not the prompt. Both were done (prompt clause + wiring). But the examples are missing. I'd flag IMPORTANT.

Also requirement #3: "Never-again REG: scripted-provider test where a trivial question in a gate-active session yields zero tool calls and no checklist/ledger in the visible transcript; unfenced-ledger strip unit tests." The loop test covers trivial turn no event + strip; prompt test covers interactive×autopilot has no contract. The "gate-active session trivial Q&A → direct answer zero verification calls" is partially covered: `finalize_gate_loop_test` trivial turn asserts no event and stripping. The IT tests updated. REG: scripted-provider test where trivial question in gate-active session yields zero tool calls — is there an integration test for that? The ITs use a script with tool calls. Hmm — the unit loop test uses runTurns with just textTurn, asserts no TaskLedgerEvent. That covers "gate does not fire". Whether the model makes zero verification calls depends on the prompt, which can't be tested with a scripted provider making zero calls by construction... Actually a scripted provider CAN assert the script (requests made) contains no verification commands. The mock's bodies are the requests. In IT-1 headless, the script includes tool calls; a trivial-question IT would have a script of a single text turn and assert... the model didn't call tools — trivially true with scripted provider unless script has tool turns. The real check is the prompt content test (interactive has no contract). For headless trivial question: prompt carries the clause; the scripted provider wouldn't call tools anyway. So the meaningful REG is the prompt test + unit loop test. Reasonably covered.

N. Check `headlessRun` in AgentCliConfig and other hosts (flutter_app AgentService) — does the app ever run headless-ish? Gate default off; fine.

O. **Perf**: `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` calls `_parseLedgerItems` for each span (reversed) — and then `parseTaskLedger` calls `_parseLedgerItems` AGAIN on the winning span, and `stripTaskLedger` re-runs `_ledgerSpans` + `_parseLedgerItems` again. So a text with K spans gets parsed ~2-3×. Minor. Also `_emitFinalizeGateFold` calls `parseTaskLedger` then `stripTaskLedger` on the same block → duplicate work. SUGGESTION.

P. **`_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` heading-with-no-entries case**: "A heading with no entries spans itself only" — then `_parseLedgerItems('')` is empty → not parseable → `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` skips it. But in `_ledgerSpans`, that empty span is still added and `nextLine = j` where j advanced past blanks... wait if heading has no entries, the while loop: first line after heading, if blank → continue (body stays empty, lastEntry stays i). Then prose line → break. nextLine = j (the prose line index)? No — break happens at j pointing to prose, nextLine=j. OK. But blanks between heading and prose are consumed via nextLine — irrelevant since the span wasn't parseable and strip won't run (strip uses `_lastParseableLedgerSpan`). Fine.

BUT: consider heading with no requirement entries but with OTHER bullets: `## task-ledger\n- some unrelated note\n` → body=['- some unrelated note'], `_parseLedgerItems` — entry match: key='some', value='unrelated note'. Then flush: does the item have a requirement? Let me check `_parseLedgerItems` — "Rows without a requirement are dropped". So `- some unrelated note` has key `some`, no `requirement` key → dropped → items empty → not parseable ✓ (test covers this).

Q. **False positive: entry line regex in prose**: `## task-ledger` heading followed by a normal bullet list like:

```
## task-ledger
- requirement: the user asked about the ledger format
```

would parse as a ledger with requirement text — tolerant by design. Fine.

R. Now the **context message identity rewrite (G)** — critical to verify. Let me read the agent_loop around where newMessages get appended to context, and how CLI persists assistant messages.

Also S: **`currentContext.messages`** — is it a growable list that the session persists from? If the fold mutates `contextMessages[at] = fold.stripped!` AFTER the message was already persisted to disk (session JSONL), the disk record keeps the unstripped version while in-memory is stripped. The CLI persists assistant messages when? Via AgentListener events (MessageEvent?) — agent_cli subscribes and appends records. Need to check: does the CLI persist the assistant message record before the fold (during streaming) or after run completes? If the transcript on disk shows the ledger, the "transcript never shows it" claim fails for persisted sessions (resume would show it). Let me investigate.

Let me look at agent_loop.dart around the fold call site and how messages flow.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Title**: gh-1516 [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1516` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +538
- **Deletions**: -125
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T21:57:47Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T23:04:38Z

## PR Description

Closes #1516
## gh-1516: FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions

### Root Cause
The FinalizeGate was keyed on the approval **mode** (`approvalMode == unattended`) as a proxy for attendance. Autopilot in an interactive TUI is attended, yet `agent_cli.dart` + `agent_cli_prompt.dart` turned the full gh-1412 verification contract on — the model ran the checklist ritual on every answer, and the unfenced `task-ledger` near-miss shape was neither parsed nor stripped, so it rendered as transcript garbage.

### Fix
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`, `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart`: gate + contract now key on `config.headlessRun` (attendance: `fa -p`/bench) — interactive sessions stay gate-free under **every** approval mode.
- `prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (+ regenerated `prompts.g.dart`): trivial-turn clause — pure Q&A (no produced state) answers directly, no checklist/ledger.
- `lib/src/agent/finalize_gate.dart`: tolerant `parseTaskLedger` (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullets) and new `stripTaskLedger` (fenced or unfenced).
- `lib/src/agent/agent_loop.dart`: `_foldTaskLedger` — no tool calls in the run ⇒ gate does not fire (no `TaskLedgerEvent`); whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it.

### Test Coverage
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` — interactive×autopilot has NO contract (RED before fix); headless×any mode carries it.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` — tolerant-strip unit tests: unfenced/bold-heading parse, fenced-wins, strip of both shapes, prose false-positives rejected.
- `test/agent/finalize_gate_loop_test.dart` — trivial turn: no event + over-eager ledger still stripped; produced-state turn: event + stripped message; unfenced near-miss fires the gate.
- `test/cli/finalize_gate_ledger_persist_test.dart`, `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` — updated to the attendance semantics (IT-1 headless keeps the full gh-1412 contract; IT-2 interactive autopilot persists no ledger).
- Full suite (`dart test` minus integration/llm/pty/browser-ext/io/perf tags): 10144 passed, 0 failed (one unrelated flake in a first run, green on two reruns); finalize-gate ITs pass with `--tags integration`.

### Notes
- Bench behavior unchanged: bench runs are `fa -p` → `headlessRun` true → full contract.
- `fa wire-serve` (not a `-p` run) keeps the gate off regardless of approval mode; flag in review if wire runs should count as unattended.
- Skipped the optional `agent.finalizeGate: on|off|auto` config knob — default `auto` (headless-only) is the whole fix; add the knob only if a concrete need appears.

# gh-1516: [BUG] FinalizeGate leaks into interactive sessions: approvalMode=autopilot turns on unattended verification ritual + visible task-ledger garbage (gh-1412 regression)

## Description

## Symptom (owner report, session 01a12772-de61-77e1-b3c9-332394827a86, ai_conf/demo)

Interactive TUI, `approvalMode: autopilot`, trivial question ("почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"):

- verification ritual around a plain-text answer: writes its own reply to `/tmp/fa_reply.txt`, `sed` it back, `stat -f %m` both files to "measure response time" — 4+ pointless shell calls, several as background jobs;
- the reply carries a visible "Checklist (требования и верификация)" section and an **unfenced `task-ledger` dump** (requirement/command/expected/actual/status).

Same setup with haiku answered the same class of question normally — so the trigger is universal, the explosion is model-dependent (weak models take imperative prompts literally).

## Root cause (owner direction: the PROMPT, not the mode wiring)

`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md` (gh-1412) says "Before ANY final summary you MUST: checklist → verify each item with a real command → ledger" with **no scoping by turn type**. "Verify produced state" presumes the model can judge that a pure chat turn produced no state — gpt-5-mini can't; it verifies the act of answering itself. The prompt never says when the contract does NOT apply.

(Secondary, kept for completeness: the gate is wired to `approvalMode == unattended` at agent_cli.dart:649 — but per owner direction the fix belongs in the prompt: a chat turn must not trigger the ritual in ANY mode.)

## Requirement

1. **Self-scoping prompt**: finalize_gate.md opens with an explicit applicability rule — the contract applies ONLY to turns that produced artifacts or state changes (files written/edited, commands that mutate, services/configs touched). Pure discussion / Q&A / explanations / status answers → answer directly, NO checklist, NO verification commands, NO ledger. Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a "why did you…" question, a "what does X do" question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules.
2. **Tolerant strip**: `finalize_gate.dart` must also catch the near-miss shapes models actually emit (unfenced `task-ledger` heading + bullet list) — parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown.
3. Never-again REG: scripted-provider test where a trivial question in a gate-active session yields zero tool calls and no checklist/ledger in the visible transcript; unfenced-ledger strip unit tests.

## Acceptance

- Gate-active session (any mode): trivial Q&A → direct answer, zero verification calls, clean transcript.
- Gate-active session with real produced state: full gh-1412 contract intact (checklist, real verification, fenced ledger parsed + persisted).
- Bench/unattended behavior for real tasks unchanged.
