# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

A. **`stripTaskLedger` / parseTaskLedger double scanning**: `_emitFinalizeGateFold` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)`, each runs `_ledgerSpans` (O(n)). Minor perf, negligible for final answers. Also parse called per text block.

B. **`_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` blank tolerance**: blanks "may separate entries", but the loop breaks on the FIRST non-blank non-entry line. Consider:

```
## task-ledger
- requirement: a
  command: x

some prose paragraph

- requirement: b
```

The scan breaks at "some prose paragraph" and the span ends at requirement a. Then `- requirement: b` later is a dangling entry — never included. This means the last ledger of the doc could be only partial. Also, the `_entryLine` regex `^\s*-\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` matches any bullet with `key: value` — e.g. a regular markdown bullet "- requirement: see the docs" in normal prose right after a `## task-ledger` heading would be parsed. That's the intended tolerant behavior though.

C. **More serious**: `_entryLine` matches at ANY indentation, including deeper-indented bullets that are part of a list item's nested content. Also `_fieldLine` `^\s+([A-Za-z_]+)\s*:\s?(.*)$` requires at least one leading whitespace — matches any indented line with `key: value`... wait, it would also match `  - requirement: x`? No, `- requirement` starts with `-` not a letter. OK.

Actually the pre-existing parse had the same grammar inside the fence; the tolerance extends it outside. Prose false-positive test exists ("the task-ledger record is persisted hidden" — inline, rejected since token must be alone on line). Good.

D. **`_isLedgerHeading`**: `token = line.trim()`, handles `#` prefix strip via regex `'^#{1,6}\s*'`. What about heading like `## **task-ledger**` (bold inside heading)? Not handled — token after `#` strip = `**task-ledger**`, then bold check handles it. Order: strip `#` first, then bold. Good. What about `###task-ledger` (no space)? `^#{1,6}\s*` matches zero spaces, so `###task-ledger` → `task-ledger` ✓.

E. **Blank-line runaway in `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt`**: blanks are skipped but never end the span — so:

```
## task-ledger
- requirement: a
  command: x
  status: pass

(the agent continues writing many paragraphs…)

- requirement: stray mention: something
```

The scan breaks at first prose line. OK fine.

But wait — a subtle bug: blanks are consumed inside the while loop without updating `lastEntry`, and the scan only ends at a non-blank non-entry line or EOF. That means the span `nextLine = j` could skip blank lines and the strip removes [startLine, lastEntry]. Fine.

F. **`stripTaskLedger` blank-collapse behavior mutates surrounding text**: it collapses ALL blank runs in the whole answer (not just around the removal site). Original:

```

Para 2 (double blank between paragraphs)
```

It's a behavioral wart: the final answer text gets reformatted beyond the ledger removal. For a "transcript never shows it" requirement, it changes the visible answer formatting. Probably IMPORTANT at most — it's a minor cosmetic overreach. Hmm, but the doc comment says "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated" — the implementation collapses ALL runs, not just the removal site. That's a discrepancy between comment and code. blocks.text:
Confirmed the full picture: the ledger text is **streamed live** to stdout (`_onTextDelta` → `io.write`) and **persisted on disk** (`_persistIncremental` on `MessageEndEvent`) BEFORE `_emitFinalizeGateFold` runs at end-of-run. The fold only rewrites the in-memory `newMessages`/`context.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. So:

1. `fa -p` stdout shows the full ledger (streamed live) — the fold can't un-stream it.
2. The session JSONL assistant record retains the ledger — resume replays it into the model's context; `fa trajectory`/attach/bench log sync show it.

The PR's claim "the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it" holds only for the event payload. This is the central feature of the PR's requirement #2 ("never leave it in the transcript") — materially not achieved for the persisted/observable transcript.

Hmm, but is that truly a defect the author should fix, or is streaming/live-persistence inherently impossible to strip? The natural fix: perform the fold BEFORE the final MessageEndEvent is emitted / before persistence. Since the loop knows the message is final only after the tool phase decides to stop, one approach: restructure so that when the run ends on an assistant message, the fold is applied to the message before `MessageEndEvent` is emitted... but MessageEndEvent fires inside `_finishStreamed` immediately. Alternative: in gate mode, buffer... complex. Another approach: after the fold, update the persisted record — the session repo is append-only JSONL, but there may be a repair path. Alternatively the CLI could defer persisting the LAST assistant message until AgentEndEvent (when gate on). Or: strip at the SOURCE — in `_finishStreamed`, before emitting MessageEndEvent... but "final" isn't known yet (tool calls may follow).

Hmm wait — actually there's a subtlety: if the message has tool calls, its text (which may contain a ledger? no — ledger only in final text answer). The fold targets the terminal message. If the terminal message has NO tool calls, then when it's added... the loop adds it via newMessages.add(message) at line 1114, then `_terminalRunMessages`, then tool phase: if no tool calls, hasMoreToolCalls false → loop continues → breaks at `break` when no pending messages. Only THEN do we know it's final.

Simplest correct approach: move the fold to right after the loop determines termination but BEFORE `AgentEndEvent`... that's where it is. The problem is downstream consumers already saw/persisted the message. To make persistence see the stripped version, `_persistIncremental` would need to run after the fold — i.e., persist the final assistant message lazily. Or the fold could be computed EAGERLY: strip the ledger from EVERY assistant text message as it finalizes when the gate is on? No — stripping mid-run text would remove ledgers the model quotes for its own continuation... Actually would that be bad? The contract says ledger goes at the END of the final answer. If we strip every text block at MessageEndEvent time when gate is on (before persisting/rendering), then: mid-run assistant messages with tool calls rarely contain ledgers; if one did, stripping it removes self-check info from context the model might reference — but the model already produced it; the hidden record only persists the FINAL one. Hmm, but then the TaskLedgerEvent emission at end-of-run would parse from newMessages — already stripped! So they'd need to capture the ledger before stripping. Feasible: in `_finishStreamed` (or the fold), parse ledger from the raw text before strip, stash it, strip before MessageEndEvent emit when gate on... but wait, the model's NEXT request context would then lack the ledger — which is exactly the desired "transcript never shows it".

But careful: stripping at finalize-time changes what the MODEL sees in its own context for multi-round runs — the ledger from round N would vanish before round N+1. The contract wants the ledger only in the final answer anyway.

This is a design-level fix; for the review I flag the gap clearly with the evidence and let the author choose. Given the machine protocol, this is a correctness bug in the claimed behavior → BLOCKING.

Wait, let me reconsider whether to call this BLOCKING vs IMPORTANT. The gate only fires on headless runs. For bench runs, is the ledger in the JSONL assistant record harmful? The bench summary parses the hidden `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` counts; no ledger → `checklist: none`) — unaffected. The transcript garbage matters for... the owner cares about "transcript garbage" interactive sessions — now gate-free. For headless, the JSONL ledger is arguably harmless audit info. BUT the PR explicitly implements stripping with tests asserting "the transcript never shows it", and the ticket requirement 2 says "never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown." The stripped transcript is the deliverable; it's implemented only for the in-memory/event view. The persisted JSONL (the canonical transcript of a headless run — the thing that gets synced, replayed, attached, trajectorialized) still shows it. I maintain BLOCKING — the feature doesn't deliver its stated contract on the artifact that matters most for unattended runs.

Hmm, one more consideration: maybe there's an end-of-run persist pass that rewrites? `_afterRun` "only writes anything the listener may have missed" — appends missing records, doesn't rewrite. No.

Also check `AgentEndEvent` handling: CLI doesn't persist messages from AgentEndEvent. Right.

Now let me also check the second potential issue: ticket requirement #1 missing the 2-3 concrete negative examples in the prompt. The added clause is abstract with one generic parenthetical. The ticket: "Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a 'why did you…' question, a 'what does X do' question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules." This is an explicit ticket requirement not met. IMPORTANT (ticket AC gap).

Wait — but also consider: does the prompt fix even matter now? Interactive sessions are gate-free under all modes (the real regression fix). The prompt clause is the second layer for headless trivial turns. The ticket's owner direction was prompt-first; the PR did both. The examples are still missing → IMPORTANT.

Next: `stripTaskLedger` global blank-collapse — the doc says collapse removal-site runs, implementation collapses ALL blank runs and trims the whole answer edges. Deviation; low impact → SUGGESTION. Actually let me re-read:

```dart
final collapsed = <String>[];
for (final line in kept) {
  if (line.trim().isEmpty && (collapsed.isEmpty || collapsed.last.trim().isEmpty)) continue;
  collapsed.add(line);
}
while (collapsed.isNotEmpty && collapsed.first.trim().isEmpty) collapsed.removeAt(0);
return collapsed.join('\n').trimRight();
```

Yes — every blank run in the whole answer collapses to one blank, leading blanks removed, trailing trimmed. If the model intentionally used double blank lines (markdown paragraph separation is single blank, but lists/sections may use more), the stripped answer differs beyond the ledger. SUGGESTION (or IMPORTANT-lite). I'll go SUGGESTION... Actually the claim in the comment: "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated" — 'them' = "blank runs behind" the removal site. The code doesn't localize. Given final answers with meaningful double-blank formatting are rare and impact is cosmetic, SUGGESTION.

Next: `_emitFinalizeGateFold` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)` — each re-scans and re-parses (O(spans × lines) ×2, plus `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` parses each span body). Could compute span once. SUGGESTION (perf nit).

Next: `producedState` = any tool call in run — includes read-only calls; prompt says "ran no state-changing commands". The persist test uses a `read` call to qualify. This mismatch means a read-only turn (e.g. the model just read a file to answer a question, then emitted an over-eager ledger) fires TaskLedgerEvent → hidden record persisted. Is that harmful? Minor. Also the ticket AC "trivial Q&A → zero tool calls" — zero tool calls remains the gate.…

So `headlessRun` = `headlessPrompt != null` — true only for `fa -p`/positional prompt. `fa wire-serve` keeps `headlessRun: false` (config built once before the wire-serve branch) → gate off for wire-serve, as the PR notes explicitly. Bench uses `fa -p` → gate on. Consistent with the PR description.

Note: `_runWireServeHost` — wire serve is genuinely unattended, but the PR flags this as a conscious decision asking reviewers. Also `fa hub serve` / `fa dap`? Those don't create an AgentCli probably. And `runWireServeHost` runs the SAME cli with headlessRun=false — so interactive-REPL semantics. OK — it's a deliberate, documented open question → SUGGESTION-level note (the PR itself invites the flag).

Also, what about `fa serve --attach` / headless wake runs (idle inbox wake launches headless run)? Wake launcher — "mail to an asleep session already launches a headless wake run that drains the inbox" — how is that run launched? Probably `fa -p`-like → headlessRun true → gate ON for a wake run in a session that was interactive. Hmm — a wake-launched headless run of an INTERACTIVE session: the FinalizeGate contract prompt gets appended (system prompt composed with config.headlessRun=true) even though the session is primarily interactive. Is that a problem? The wake run is genuinely unattended (no human watching), so the gate firing is semantically right. Prompt difference between wake runs and REPL runs in the same session is a minor inconsistency; acceptable.

Now — the in-memory fold and `_agent.state.messages`. After the run, Agent.addAll(newMessages) presumably replaces state; stripped message lands there ✓.

One more check on `_foldTaskLedger`: `producedState` scans `messages` = newMessages — includes ToolCall blocks in ANY assistant message of the run ✓. But `messages` also includes `prompts` (newMessages initialized with `[...prompts]`) — prompts are user/system messages, fine.

Edge: multi-block final message with ledger in a NON-last text block — loop scans reversed, first parseable wins, earlier ones not stripped. Old behavior identical (first parseable from reversed). ✓ consistent with "last block wins" doc.

Edge in `_fencedLedgerSpanAt`: a fenced block whose closing fence is a ```task-ledger opening? `_fenceLine.hasMatch` treats ANY fence line as closing. If a model opens a second task-ledger fence inside... rare. Pre-existing semantics.

Edge: `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` — a `## task-ledger` heading followed IMMEDIATELY (no blank) by prose that matches `_fieldLine` (indented `key: value`)? e.g. nested indented content. Tolerant by design.

One more potential correctness issue: `_isLedgerHeading` — what about a heading line `## task-ledger extra words`? token = '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' ≠ 'task-ledger' → not heading ✓.

What about `#### task-ledger` (7 hashes)? `^#{1,6}\s*` on '#### task-ledger' — matches 6 hashes then requires `\s*` — next char is '#', not whitespace... `\s*` matches empty, so replace removes '######' leaving '# task-ledger' → not equal → false negative. Fine (7-hash isn't a heading anyway).

Now — the `_SpanScan`/span scanning and `stripTaskLedger` interplay when the parseable span is NOT the last span: `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` returns the last PARSEABLE span; strip removes exactly that span's lines ✓. But subtle: if the last span is parseable but an EARLIER span is not, fine. If the last span is NOT parseable (e.g. heading with no requirement-bearing entries) but an earlier one is, strip removes the earlier one and leaves the near-empty later heading — acceptable.

Another subtle strip bug: for the UNFENCED span, `endLine = lastEntry` — but the scan consumed trailing BLANK lines without including them in the span (nextLine = j past blanks? No: blanks are consumed by `j++` in the loop; when a prose line breaks, nextLine = that prose line. So blanks between last entry and prose are NOT part of the span (span ends at lastEntry) but ARE skipped by the scanner. For strip, lines after lastEntry up to nextLine-1 (blanks) are KEPT in `kept` — then the global blank-collapse trims/collapses. Result is OK visually.

But what if blanks separate the heading from the first entry, and the ledger is at the END of the answer: `Answer\n## task-ledger\n- requirement: ...\n...status: pass\n` — span = heading..lastEntry. Strip removes those lines; kept = ['Answer', '', '']... wait kept includes the blank before heading and the blank between heading and first entry is INSIDE the span (span starts at heading line; the blank after heading is between startLine and endLine → removed ✓). kept = ['Answer', ''] → collapse → ['Answer'] + trimRight → 'Answer' ✓.

The natural fix: perform the fold BEFORE the final MessageEndEvent is emitted / before persistence. Since the loop knows the message is final only after the tool phase decides to stop, one approach: restructure so that when the run ends on an assistant message, the fold is applied to the message before `MessageEndEvent` is emitted... but MessageEndEvent fires inside `_finishStreamed` immediately. Alternatively the CLI could defer persisting the LAST assistant message until AgentEndEvent (when gate on). Or: strip at the SOURCE — in `_finishStreamed`, before emitting MessageEndEvent... but "final" isn't known yet (tool calls may follow).

Hmm wait — actually there's a subtlety: if the message has tool calls, its text (which may contain a ledger? no — ledger only in final text answer). The fold targets the terminal message. If the terminal message has NO tool calls, then when it's added... the loop adds it via newMessages.add(message) at line 1114, then `_terminalRunMessages`, then tool phase: if no tool calls, hasMoreToolCalls false → loop continues → breaks at `break` when no pending messages. Only THEN do we know it's final.

Simplest correct approach: move the fold to right after the loop determines termination but BEFORE `AgentEndEvent`... that's where it is. The problem is downstream consumers already saw/persisted the message. To make persistence see the stripped version, `_persistIncremental` would need to run after the fold — i.e., persist the final assistant message lazily. Or the fold could be computed EAGERLY: strip the ledger from EVERY assistant text message as it finalizes when the gate is on? No — stripping mid-run text would remove ledgers the model quotes for its own continuation... Actually would that be bad? The contract says ledger goes at the END of the final answer. If we strip every text block at MessageEndEvent time when gate is on (before persisting/rendering), then: mid-run assistant messages with tool calls rarely contain ledgers; if one did, stripping it removes self-check info from context the model might reference — but the model already produced it; the hidden record only persists the FINAL one. Hmm, but then the TaskLedgerEvent emission at end-of-run would parse from newMessages — already stripped! So they'd need to capture the ledger before stripping. Feasible: in `_finishStreamed` (or the fold), parse ledger from the raw text before strip, stash it, strip before MessageEndEvent emit when gate on... but wait, the model's NEXT request context would then lack the ledger — which is exactly the desired "transcript never shows it".

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `stripTaskLedger` rewrites the whole answer's whitespace, not just the removal site**

The doc comment says "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated", but the implementation collapses **every** blank-line run in the answer to a single blank and trims leading blanks of the whole text (`collapsed.join('\n').trimRight()` plus the leading-blank loop). Low impact (final answers rarely carry meaningful multi-blank formatting, and the fenced/unfenced shapes are at the tail), but the visible answer is user-facing text — consider limiting the collapse to the span's immediate neighborhood: remove `[startLine, endLine]`, then collapse at most the blank runs that touch the vacated range, leaving the rest of the answer byte-identical.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `stripTaskLedger` rewrites the whole answer's whitespace, not just the removal site**

The doc comment says "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated", but the implementation collapses **every** blank-line run in the answer to a single blank and trims leading blanks of the whole text (`collapsed.join('\n').trimRight()` plus the leading-blank loop). An answer that intentionally used double blank lines between sections, or leading blank lines, comes out reformatted even though only the ledger lines were removed.

Low impact (final answers rarely carry meaningful multi-blank formatting, and the fenced/unfenced shapes are at the tail), but the visible answer is user-facing text — consider limiting the collapse to the span's immediate neighborhood: remove `[startLine, endLine]`, then collapse at most the blank runs that touch the vacated range, leaving the rest of the answer byte-identical.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the fold scans and parses the answer text three times**

`_foldTaskLedger` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` and then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)`; each call re-runs `_ledgerSpans` (a full line scan), and `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` additionally runs `_parseLedgerItems` on every candidate span in reverse order — so the winning span's entries are parsed twice more inside `parseTaskLedger`/`stripTaskLedger`'s own calls. For a pathological answer with many candidate spans this is quadratic-ish and purely redundant.

Consider exposing one helper that returns the winning `_LedgerSpan` (and its parsed `TaskLedger`) once, and deriving both the event payload and the stripped text from it — e.g. `stripTaskLedger` accepting an optional pre-resolved span. Not a correctness issue at these sizes; just dead work on every gated run.

blocks.text:
Confirmed the full picture: the ledger text is **streamed live** to stdout (`_onTextDelta` → `io.write`) and **persisted on disk** (`_persistIncremental` on `MessageEndEvent`) BEFORE `_emitFinalizeGateFold` runs at end-of-run. The fold only rewrites the in-memory `newMessages`/`context.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. So:

1. `fa -p` stdout shows the full ledger (streamed live) — the fold can't un-stream it.
2. The session JSONL assistant record retains the ledger — resume replays it into the model's context; `fa trajectory`/attach/bench log sync show it.

The PR's claim "the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it" holds only for the event payload. This is the central feature of the PR's requirement #2 ("never leave it in the transcript") — materially not achieved for the persisted/observable transcript.

Hmm, but is that truly a defect the author should fix, or is streaming/live-persistence inherently impossible to strip? The natural fix: perform the fold BEFORE the final MessageEndEvent is emitted / before persistence. Since the loop knows the message is final only after the tool phase decides to stop, one approach: restructure so that when the run ends on an assistant message, the fold is applied to the message before `MessageEndEvent` is emitted... but MessageEndEvent fires inside `_finishStreamed` immediately. Alternative: in gate mode, buffer... complex. Another approach: after the fold, update the persisted record — the session repo is append-only JSONL, but there may be a repair path. Alternatively the CLI could defer persisting the LAST assistant message until AgentEndEvent (when gate on). Or: strip at the SOURCE — in `_finishStreamed`, before emitting MessageEndEvent... but "final" isn't known yet (tool calls may follow).

Hmm wait — actually there's a subtlety: if the message has tool calls, its text (which may contain a ledger? no — ledger only in final text answer). The fold targets the terminal message. If the terminal message has NO tool calls, then when it's added... the loop adds it via newMessages.add(message) at line 1114, then `_terminalRunMessages`, then tool phase: if no tool calls, hasMoreToolCalls false → loop continues → breaks at `break` when no pending messages. Only THEN do we know it's final.

Simplest correct approach: move the fold to right after the loop determines termination but BEFORE `AgentEndEvent`... that's where it is. The problem is downstream consumers already saw/persisted the message. To make persistence see the stripped version, `_persistIncremental` would need to run after the fold — i.e., persist the final assistant message lazily. Or the fold could be computed EAGERLY: strip the ledger from EVERY assistant text message as it finalizes when the gate is on? No — stripping mid-run text would remove ledgers the model quotes for its own continuation... Actually would that be bad? The contract says ledger goes at the END of the final answer. If we strip every text block at MessageEndEvent time when gate is on (before persisting/rendering), then: mid-run assistant messages with tool calls rarely contain ledgers; if one did, stripping it removes self-check info from context the model might reference — but the model already produced it; the hidden record only persists the FINAL one. Hmm, but then the TaskLedgerEvent emission at end-of-run would parse from newMessages — already stripped! So they'd need to capture the ledger before stripping. Feasible: in `_finishStreamed` (or the fold), parse ledger from the raw text before strip, stash it, strip before MessageEndEvent emit when gate on... but wait, the model's NEXT request context would then lack the ledger — which is exactly the desired "transcript never shows it".

But careful: stripping at finalize-time changes what the MODEL sees in its own context for multi-round runs — the ledger from round N would vanish before round N+1. The contract wants the ledger only in the final answer anyway.

This is a design-level fix; for the review I flag the gap clearly with the evidence and let the author choose. Given the machine protocol, this is a correctness bug in the claimed behavior → BLOCKING.

Wait, let me reconsider whether to call this BLOCKING vs IMPORTANT. The gate only fires on headless runs. For bench runs, is the ledger in the JSONL assistant record harmful? The bench summary parses the hidden `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` counts; no ledger → `checklist: none`) — unaffected. The transcript garbage matters for... the owner cares about "transcript garbage" interactive sessions — now gate-free. For headless, the JSONL ledger is arguably harmless audit info. BUT the PR explicitly implements stripping with tests asserting "the transcript never shows it", and the ticket requirement 2 says "never leave it in the transcript. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown." The stripped transcript is the deliverable; it's implemented only for the in-memory/event view. The persisted JSONL (the canonical transcript of a headless run — the thing that gets synced, replayed, attached, trajectorialized) still shows it. I maintain BLOCKING — the feature doesn't deliver its stated contract on the artifact that matters most for unattended runs.

Hmm, one more consideration: maybe there's an end-of-run persist pass that rewrites? `_afterRun` "only writes anything the listener may have missed" — appends missing records, doesn't rewrite. No.

Also check `AgentEndEvent` handling: CLI doesn't persist messages from AgentEndEvent. Right.

Now let me also check the second potential issue: ticket requirement #1 missing the 2-3 concrete negative examples in the prompt. The added clause is abstract with one generic parenthetical. The ticket: "Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a 'why did you…' question, a 'what does X do' question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules." This is an explicit ticket requirement not met. IMPORTANT (ticket AC gap).

Wait — but also consider: does the prompt fix even matter now? Interactive sessions are gate-free under all modes (the real regression fix). The prompt clause is the second layer for headless trivial turns. The ticket's owner direction was prompt-first; the PR did both. The examples are still missing → IMPORTANT.

Next: `stripTaskLedger` global blank-collapse — the doc says collapse removal-site runs, implementation collapses ALL blank runs and trims the whole answer edges. Deviation; low impact → SUGGESTION. Actually let me re-read:

```dart
final collapsed = <String>[];
for (final line in kept) {
  if (line.trim().isEmpty && (collapsed.isEmpty || collapsed.last.trim().isEmpty)) continue;
  collapsed.add(line);
}
while (collapsed.isNotEmpty && collapsed.first.trim().isEmpty) collapsed.removeAt(0);
return collapsed.join('\n').trimRight();
```

Yes — every blank run in the whole answer collapses to one blank, leading blanks removed, trailing trimmed. If the model intentionally used double blank lines (markdown paragraph separation is single blank, but lists/sections may use more), the stripped answer differs beyond the ledger. SUGGESTION (or IMPORTANT-lite). I'll go SUGGESTION... Actually the claim in the comment: "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated" — 'them' = "blank runs behind" the removal site. The code doesn't localize. Given final answers with meaningful double-blank formatting are rare and impact is cosmetic, SUGGESTION.

Next: `_emitFinalizeGateFold` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)` — each re-scans and re-parses (O(spans × lines) ×2, plus `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` parses each span body). Could compute span once. SUGGESTION (perf nit).

Next: `producedState` = any tool call in run — includes read-only calls; prompt says "ran no state-changing commands". The persist test uses a `read` call to qualify. This mismatch means a read-only turn (e.g. the model just read a file to answer a question, then emitted an over-eager ledger) fires TaskLedgerEvent → hidden record persisted. Is that harmful? Minor. Also the ticket AC "trivial Q&A → zero tool calls" — zero tool calls remains the gate.…

Edge: multi-block final message with ledger in a NON-last text block — loop scans reversed, first parseable wins, earlier ones not stripped. Old behavior identical (first parseable from reversed). ✓ consistent with "last block wins" doc.

Edge in `_fencedLedgerSpanAt`: a fenced block whose closing fence is a ```task-ledger opening? `_fenceLine.hasMatch` treats ANY fence line as closing. If a model opens a second task-ledger fence inside... rare. Pre-existing semantics.

Edge: `_unfencedLedgerSpanAt` — a `## task-ledger` heading followed IMMEDIATELY (no blank) by prose that matches `_fieldLine` (indented `key: value`)? e.g. nested indented content. Tolerant by design.

One more potential correctness issue: `_isLedgerHeading` — what about a heading line `## task-ledger extra words`? token = '[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]' ≠ 'task-ledger' → not heading ✓.

What about `#### task-ledger` (7 hashes)? `^#{1,6}\s*` on '#### task-ledger' — matches 6 hashes then requires `\s*` — next char is '#', not whitespace... `\s*` matches empty, so replace removes '######' leaving '# task-ledger' → not equal → false negative. Fine (7-hash isn't a heading anyway).

Now — the `_SpanScan`/span scanning and `stripTaskLedger` interplay when the parseable span is NOT the last span: `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` returns the last PARSEABLE span; strip removes exactly that span's lines ✓. But subtle: if the last span is parseable but an EARLIER span is not, fine. If the last span is NOT parseable (e.g. heading with no requirement-bearing entries) but an earlier one is, strip removes the earlier one and leaves the near-empty later heading — acceptable.

Another subtle strip bug: for the UNFENCED span, `endLine = lastEntry` — but the scan consumed trailing BLANK lines without including them in the span (nextLine = j past blanks? No: blanks are consumed by `j++` in the loop; when a prose line breaks, nextLine = that prose line. So blanks between last entry and prose are NOT part of the span (span ends at lastEntry) but ARE skipped by the scanner. For strip, lines after lastEntry up to nextLine-1 (blanks) are KEPT in `kept` — then the global blank-collapse trims/collapses. Result is OK visually.

But what if blanks separate the heading from the first entry, and the ledger is at the END of the answer: `Answer\n## task-ledger\n- requirement: ...\n...status: pass\n` — span = heading..lastEntry. Strip removes those lines; kept = ['Answer', '', '']... wait kept includes the blank before heading and the blank between heading and first entry is INSIDE the span (span starts at heading line; the blank after heading is between startLine and endLine → removed ✓). kept = ['Answer', ''] → collapse → ['Answer'] + trimRight → 'Answer' ✓.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn produced no artifacts and ran no state-changing commands (a pure question answered from what you already know), there is nothing to verify — skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

1. `fa -p` stdout shows the full ledger (streamed live) — the fold can't un-stream it.
2. The session JSONL assistant record retains the ledger — resume replays it into the model's context; `fa trajectory`/attach/bench log sync show it.

The PR's claim "the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it" holds only for the event payload. This is the central feature of the PR's requirement #2 ("never leave it in the transcript") — materially not achieved for the persisted/observable transcript.

Hmm, but is that truly a defect the author should fix, or is streaming/live-persistence inherently impossible to strip? The natural fix: perform the fold BEFORE the final MessageEndEvent is emitted / before persistence. Since the loop knows the message is final only after the tool phase decides to stop, one approach: restructure so that when the run ends on an assistant message, the fold is applied to the message before `MessageEndEvent` is emitted... but MessageEndEvent fires inside `_finishStreamed` immediately. Alternative: in gate mode, buffer... complex. Another approach: after the fold, update the persisted record — the session repo is append-only JSONL, but there may be a repair path. Alternatively the CLI could defer persisting the LAST assistant message until AgentEndEvent (when gate on). Or: strip at the SOURCE — in `_finishStreamed`, before emitting MessageEndEvent... but "final" isn't known yet (tool calls may follow).

Hmm wait — actually there's a subtlety: if the message has tool calls, its text (which may contain a ledger? no — ledger only in final text answer). The fold targets the terminal message. If the terminal message has NO tool calls, then when it's added... the loop adds it via newMessages.add(message) at line 1114, then `_terminalRunMessages`, then tool phase: if no tool calls, hasMoreToolCalls false → loop continues → breaks at `break` when no pending messages. Only THEN do we know it's final.

Simplest correct approach: move the fold to right after the loop determines termination but BEFORE `AgentEndEvent`... that's where it is. The problem is downstream consumers already saw/persisted the message. To make persistence see the stripped version, `_persistIncremental` would need to run after the fold — i.e., persist the final assistant message lazily. Or the fold could be computed EAGERLY: strip the ledger from EVERY assistant text message as it finalizes when the gate is on? No — stripping mid-run text would remove ledgers the model quotes for its own continuation... Actually would that be bad? The contract says ledger goes at the END of the final answer. If we strip every text block at MessageEndEvent time when gate is on (before persisting/rendering), then: mid-run assistant messages with tool calls rarely contain ledgers; if one did, stripping it removes self-check info from context the model might reference — but the model already produced it; the hidden record only persists the FINAL one. Hmm, but then the TaskLedgerEvent emission at end-of-run would parse from newMessages — already stripped! So they'd need to capture the ledger before stripping. Feasible: in `_finishStreamed` (or the fold), parse ledger from the raw text before strip, stash it, strip before MessageEndEvent emit when gate on... but wait, the model's NEXT request context would then lack the ledger — which is exactly the desired "transcript never shows it".

But careful: stripping at finalize-time changes what the MODEL sees in its own context for multi-round runs — the ledger from round N would vanish before round N+1. The contract wants the ledger only in the final answer anyway.

This is a design-level fix; for the review I flag the gap clearly with the evidence and let the author choose. Given the machine protocol, this is a correctness bug in the claimed behavior → BLOCKING.

The bench summary parses the hidden `task_ledger` record (`pass`/`fixed` counts; no ledger → `checklist: none`) — unaffected. The fence remains the canonical form; unfenced is stripped too, not shown." The stripped transcript is the deliverable; it's implemented only for the in-memory/event view. The persisted JSONL (the canonical transcript of a headless run — the thing that gets synced, replayed, attached, trajectorialized) still shows it. I maintain BLOCKING — the feature doesn't deliver its stated contract on the artifact that matters most for unattended runs.

Hmm, one more consideration: maybe there's an end-of-run persist pass that rewrites? `_afterRun` "only writes anything the listener may have missed" — appends missing records, doesn't rewrite. No.

Also check `AgentEndEvent` handling: CLI doesn't persist messages from AgentEndEvent. Right.

The ticket: "Include 2-3 negative examples in the prompt (a 'why did you…' question, a 'what does X do' question) — weak models follow examples better than abstract rules." This is an explicit ticket requirement not met. IMPORTANT (ticket AC gap).

Wait — but also consider: does the prompt fix even matter now? Interactive sessions are gate-free under all modes (the real regression fix). {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: the strip runs after the message was already persisted and rendered — the transcript still shows the ledger**

The fold at `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages` / `currentContext.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By the time it runs, two consumers have already seen the unstripped ledger:

1. **Live render** — the CLI streams answer deltas via `_onTextDelta` (`approval_commands.dart:1292`) and prints the buffered answer in `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` on `MessageEndEvent`. The fold cannot un-print text that already reached stdout.
2. **Session persistence** — `_persistIncremental` (`agent_cli_persist.dart:12`) appends every `MessageEndEvent` message to the session JSONL immediately. The final assistant record on disk therefore still contains the full `task-ledger` block.

Verified empirically (scripted headless run, `read` tool call + fenced ledger answer): the persisted assistant record in the session JSONL still contains the complete unstripped ledger. Consequences:

- **Resume** replays the ledger into the model's context — the "transcript never shows it" contract is broken exactly where it matters most for unattended runs.
- `fa trajectory`, the attach view, and the bench `agent-logs/fah-sessions` sync all render the ledger from the JSONL assistant record.

This contradicts the PR description ("whenever a ledger parses, the final answer is rewritten so the transcript never shows it") and ticket requirement 2 ("parse, persist as the hidden record, never leave it in the transcript"). The existing tests don't catch it because they assert only the `AgentEndEvent` payload and the `task_ledger` custom record — never the content of the persisted assistant message record.

Possible directions (author's choice):

- Apply the strip **before** `MessageEndEvent` is emitted for a terminal message — e.g. in gate mode, parse-and-strip each assistant text block at finalize time in `_finishStreamed`, stashing the parsed ledger for the end-of-run event (mid-run blocks rarely carry a ledger, and the contract only sanctions one in the final answer anyway).
- Or defer persistence of the final assistant record until the fold has run (the session repo is append-only, but the CLI already has record-pruning machinery from the checkpoint/rewind path that could rewrite the tail).
- Whichever route: add a test that reads the persisted session JSONL and asserts the last assistant record contains no `task-ledger`, so this can't regress.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `stripTaskLedger` rewrites the whole answer's whitespace, not just the removal site**

The doc comment says "collapse them and trim the edges the ledger vacated", but the implementation collapses **every** blank-line run in the answer to a single blank and trims leading blanks of the whole text (`collapsed.join('\n').trimRight()` plus the leading-blank loop). An answer that intentionally used double blank lines between sections, or leading blank lines, comes out reformatted even though only the ledger lines were removed.

Low impact (final answers rarely carry meaningful multi-blank formatting, and the fenced/unfenced shapes are at the tail), but the visible answer is user-facing text — consider limiting the collapse to the span's immediate neighborhood: remove `[startLine, endLine]`, then collapse at most the blank runs that touch the vacated range, leaving the rest of the answer byte-identical.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: the fold scans and parses the answer text three times**

`_foldTaskLedger` calls `parseTaskLedger(block.text)` and then `stripTaskLedger(block.text)`; each call re-runs `_ledgerSpans` (a full line scan), and `_lastParseableLedgerSpan` additionally runs `_parseLedgerItems` on every candidate span in reverse order — so the winning span's entries are parsed twice more inside `parseTaskLedger`/`stripTaskLedger`'s own calls. For a pathological answer with many candidate spans this is quadratic-ish and purely redundant.

Consider exposing one helper that returns the winning `_LedgerSpan` (and its parsed `TaskLedger`) once, and deriving both the event payload and the stripped text from it — e.g. `stripTaskLedger` accepting an optional pre-resolved span. Not a correctness issue at these sizes; just dead work on every gated run.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `producedState` = any tool call, but the prompt scopes the gate to "state-changing commands"**

The loop treats a run that issued *any* tool call as producing state (`messages.any((m) => m is AssistantMessage && m.content.any((block) => block is ToolCall))`), while the new prompt clause scopes the exemption to turns that "produced no artifacts and ran no **state-changing** commands". A read-only turn — e.g. the model answers a question after one `read` call, then emits an over-eager ledger — still produces a hidden `task_ledger` record, which the prompt told the model not to produce for such turns.

The any-tool approximation is understandable (the loop can't cheaply classify which calls mutate), and the new persist test itself uses a `read` call to qualify the run. But then the prompt and the telemetry disagree about what "trivial" means. Either narrow the prompt wording to "no tool calls" (accurate, matches the implementation) or document the approximation on `producedState` so the next reader doesn't treat the divergence as a bug.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES — 1 BLOCKING · 1 IMPORTANT · 4 SUGGESTIONS

**🚨 Blocking — the ledger strip lands too late** (`agent_loop.dart:1171`). I verified empirically with a scripted headless run: `_emitFinalizeGateFold` rewrites only the in-memory `newMessages`/`context.messages` and the `AgentEndEvent` payload. By then (a) the CLI already streamed the ledger text to stdout via `_onTextDelta`, and (b) `_persistIncremental` already appended the unstripped assistant record to the session JSONL on `MessageEndEvent`. So the persisted transcript — the artifact resume, `fa trajectory`, attach views, and the bench `agent-logs` sync actually consume — still shows the ledger, contradicting the PR's central claim and ticket req #2 ("never leave it in the transcript"). The tests miss it because they assert only the event payload and the `task_ledger` custom record, never the persisted assistant record.

**⚠️ Important — ticket req #1 not fully met** (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md:7`): the ticket explicitly required 2-3 concrete negative examples ("why did you…", "what does X do…") since weak models follow examples better than rules; the added clause is abstract with a single generic parenthetical.

**💡 Suggestions**: (3) `stripTaskLedger` collapses all blank runs / trims the whole answer, not just the removal site; (4) the fold triple-scans/re-parses the answer text; (5) `producedState` = *any* tool call vs the prompt's "state-changing commands" scoping; (6) `fa wire-serve` is unattended but stays gate-free — flagged as the PR itself requested.

What's solid: the `headlessRun` re-keying is the right fix for the interactive-autopilot regression, the unfenced near-miss parsing is well-covered by unit/loop/prompt/IT tests (40/40 green locally, `dart analyze` clean on changed files), and the CRAP-ratchet rework is behavior-preserving.
